newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Hoogovens profit down but above forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Hoogovens profit down but above forecasts.

text.p: Steel and aluminium group Koninklijke Nederlandsche Hoogovens en Staalfabrieken NV announced a sharp fall in 1996 net profit on Thursday, but the figures were well above expectations and the firm said it was positive about 1997, sending the shares higher.
Net profit in 1996 was 326 million guilders ($169 million), way down from 1995's 507 million guilders, but comfortably above the analysts' forecast range of 260 million to 310 million.
The company said earnings had been hit by lower metals selling prices, while margins at the majority of processing operations had been squeezed due to lower demand for rolled and extruded products.
Group turnover dipped to 7.93 billion guilders from 1995's 8.10 billion and the company maintained the dividend at 3.00 guilders per share.

The company emphasised its confidence about the current year, saying in a statement with results: "We expect that the net result from ordinary operations will improve compared to 1996 during the course of 1997."
The recovery in Europe was expected to result in moderate economic growth in 1997, which would have a positive impact on demand for steel and aluminium products.
"We also expect to realise high sales in 1997 and furthermore an improvement in the product mix of both our steel and aluminium products," it said.

Earnings from ordinary operations at the steel division fell to 427 million guilders in 1996 from a year-earlier 720 million. Aluminium earnings from ordinary operations dropped to 43 million in 1996 from 140 million guilders.
Although increased demand was not yet reflected in prices, it expected sales prices to rise in 1997.

Investments during the current year would be sharply higher compared with 1996, it said. "The expenditure on investment will increase considerably in 1997 compared with 1996. This relates both to investments in fixed assets and to acquisitions."

During 1997 it hoped to make a decision to invest in an integrated casting and rolling installation. "Important investments in acquisitions relate to the acquisition of the remaining 50 percent of shares in Hille & Mueller and the planned joint venture with Usines Gustave Boel," Hoogovens added.
The markets welcomed the news, sending the shares 7.00 guilders higher to 98.00 guilders, which in turn boosted the Amsterdam bourse.

Peter Wortel at Delta Lloyd Bank said the results were encouraging as the indication at the half year point was for lower numbers. "The second half showed some recovery, notably in steel prices. They're stable now, but they're up from August 1996.

"The future for Hoogovens looks good, the economy is improving, steel prices are good and financially the company is very sound. We have had it as a buy since last December and certainly if these figures hold out we'll be very satisfied." ($ = 1.928 Dutch Guilders)
